knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Radical Function Using the Chain Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=7{x}^{2}+x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=14x+1.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (14x+1) \\  & =\frac{14x+1}{2\sqrt{7{x}^{2}+x}} \\  & =\frac{14x+1}{2\sqrt{7{x}^{2}+x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{-5{x}^{2}+89}$ at the point where $x=-4.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=-5{x}^{2}+89.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-10x.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (-10x) \\  & =-\frac{10x}{2\sqrt{-5{x}^{2}+89}} \\  & =-\frac{5x}{\sqrt{-5{x}^{2}+89}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=-4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-4} & ={(-\frac{5x}{\sqrt{-5{x}^{2}+89}})|}_{x=-4} \\  & =\frac{-10(-4)}{2\sqrt{-5(-4{)}^{2}+89}} \\  & =\frac{40}{2\sqrt{9}} \\  & =\frac{20}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+45}$ at the point where $x=-2.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u={x}^{2}+45.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (2x) \\  & =\frac{2x}{2\sqrt{{x}^{2}+45}} \\  & =\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+45}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=-2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-2} & ={(\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+45}})|}_{x=-2} \\  & =\frac{2(-2)}{2\sqrt{(-2{)}^{2}+45}} \\  & =\frac{-4}{2\sqrt{49}} \\  & =-\frac{2}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$
